bib.title: A Survey on Self-Evolution of Large Language Models

legacy_report:
SOURCE: A Survey on Self-Evolution of Large Language Models. Zhengwei Tao, Ting-En Lin, Xiancai Chen, Hangyu Li, Yuchuan Wu, Yongbin Li, Zhi Jin, Fei Huang, Dacheng Tao, Jingren Zhou (PKU, Alibaba, NTU). arXiv:2404.14387v2, 3 Jun 2024. Preprint.

COVERAGE: Pages 1-19 of 28 read in full (about 74,000 of 95,863 chars). That is every body section (intro, framework, objectives, §4-§8, conclusion). The remaining pages are the reference list, which I skimmed only to its start, as allowed. Confirmed by grep: the body has NO percentage results.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- The framework is one iterative cycle of four phases: experience acquisition, experience refinement, updating, evaluation. At iteration t the model has an objective E_t = (ability A_t, direction D_t) and it runs a four-step loop. (1) Acquisition: f_T makes tasks, f_Y makes solutions, f_F gets feedback. (2) Refinement: f_R filters or corrects. (3) Update: f_U gives M_{t+1}. (4) Evaluation: f_E returns the score S_t and the next objective E_{t+1}.
  number: none
  setup: conceptual, no experiments
  quote: "iterative cycle involving experience acquisition, experience refinement, updating, and evaluation" and "After updating the model in-weight or in-context, the LLM is evaluated to measure progress and set new objectives."
  where: p.2
- Formal definitions, eqs. 1-7: E^t=(A^t,D^t); T^t=f_T(E^t,M^t); Y^t=f_Y(T^t,E^t,M^t); F^t=f_F(T^t,Y^t,E^t,M^t;ENV); (T~,Y~)=f_R(T,Y,F,E,M); M^{t+1}=f_U(T~,Y~,E,M); E^{t+1},S^t=f_E(M^t,E^t,ENV).
  where: pp.4, 7, 9, 11, 12, 14, 16
- Acquisition has three parts. Task evolution is knowledge-based (structured, e.g. Self-Align, Ditto, SOLID; unstructured, e.g. UltraChat, SciGLM), knowledge-free (Self-Instruct, Evol-Instruct, MetaMath, PromptBreeder, backtranslation) or selective (random sampling, DiverseEvol, SOFT, V-STaR). Solution evolution is positive (rationale-based, interactive, self-play, grounded) or negative (contrastive, perturbative). Feedback is model-based (a score or a critique text) or environment-based (code interpreter, tool execution, embodied, other agents).
  quote: "we divide experience acquisition into three parts: task evolution, solution evolution, and obtaining feedback."
  where: p.7-12
- Refinement has two branches. Filtering is metric-based (ReST-EM binary correctness reward, AutoAct F1 and accuracy, Self-Instruct ROUGE-L dedup) or metric-free (self-consistency, LMSI, CodeT). Correcting is critique-based (Self-Refine, CAI, CRITIC, Reflexion) or critique-free (STaR rationalization, Self-Debugging).
  quote: "We classify the methods into two categories: filtering and correcting."
  where: p.12-14
- Updating is in-weight or in-context. In-weight has three families against catastrophic forgetting. Replay covers experience replay (ReST, AMIE, SOTOPIA-pi) and generative replay (SSR, SDFT). Regularization covers KL penalty (InstructGPT), Elastic Reset, WARM and AMA. Architecture covers LoRA, ConPET and merging (Model Soups, EvoLLM). In-context covers external memory (MemGPT, MemoryBank, TiM, ICE, AesopAgent) and working memory (Reflexion, IML, Agent-Pro, ProAgent). Table 2 gives memory operations as Insert, Reflect and Forget. MemGPT forgets by FIFO queue and MemoryBank by a forgetting curve on insert time.
  quote: "the core challenge lies in achieving overall improvement and preventing catastrophic forgetting"
  where: p.14-16
- Evaluation is split into quantitative (reward-model score, LLM-as-a-Judge) and qualitative (case analysis, ChatEval, TRAN's error-derived rules). The authors call it underexplored.
  quote: "how to accurately assess the performance of an evolved model and provide directions for future improvements is a crucial yet underexplored research area." Also: "compared with instance-level critic or reflection, qualitative evaluation at the task- or model-level still needs comprehensive investigation."
  where: p.16-17
- Autonomy levels. Low: the user fixes the objective E and designs every module f. Medium: the user fixes E and the model builds the modules. High: the model diagnoses its own deficiency, sets its own E from the f_E output and designs the modules. Most existing work is low-level.
  quote: "Most of the current works lie at this level." and "developing highly autonomous self-evolution frameworks remains an open problem."
  where: p.17-18
- Self-evolution stalls after a few rounds (the only quantitative-ish claim). Hypothesis offered: the self-critic has not co-evolved with the objective.
  number: three rounds
  setup: cites ReST-EM [103] and A3T [141]; no numbers given in this survey
  quote: "Recent studies [103, 141] also show that current methods struggle to improve after more than three rounds of self-evolution."
  where: p.18
- Self-correction evidence is mixed.
  number: 22 billion parameters
  quote: "Huang et al [51] observed self-corrective behavior in models with over 22 billion parameters, while Ganguli et al [38] finds LLMs struggle to self-correct reasoning errors without external feedback."
  where: p.18
- Model collapse risk. Self-generated data may reduce diversity and cause collapse. Self-consuming loops lose quality and diversity (Alemohammad et al; Fu et al). The mitigation named is balancing synthetic and real data.
  quote: "lead to 'model collapse,' where models fail to capture complex, long-tailed data distributions [100]."
  where: p.18
- Motivating anecdotes, not experiments: AMIE beats primary care physicians in diagnostic accuracy; WizardLM-2 beats the initial GPT-4. Llama-3 was trained on 15T tokens, so more real data may hit a limit.
  number: 15 trillion tokens
  quote: "Microsoft's WizardLM-2 exceeds the performance of the initial version of GPT-4"; "comprising 15 trillion tokens"
  where: p.2

OPEN PROBLEMS (section 8)
- 8.1 Objectives need diversity and hierarchy (sub-goals, e.g. tool use split into sub-dimensions).
- 8.2 Autonomy should rise from low to high.
- 8.3 Acquisition and refinement lack theory (self-correction mixed, collapse, the 3-round plateau).
- 8.4 Updating: the stability-plasticity dilemma is unresolved.
- 8.5 Evaluation needs dynamic benchmarks, because static ones go stale and models may reach test data through search. Sotopia is the example.
- 8.6 Safety and superalignment (OpenAI Superalignment, scalable oversight).

LIMITS
- It is a taxonomy only. There are no experiments, no benchmark comparisons and no ablations, and a grep for "%" found none. It reports no cost, compute or per-method scores. Do not cite it for effect sizes.
- It does not show which refinement or update choices work best.
- The 3-round plateau and the 22B threshold are second-hand citations.
- The authors concede the theory is lacking and evaluation is underexplored.
- Dated: the survey is from mid-2024 and covers STaR, ReST-EM, Self-Refine, Reflexion and similar work. It predates later reasoning-model RL, so treat the method lists as a 2024 snapshot.
- Scope is mostly weight-training self-training. The in-context and memory update parts overlap with agent loops, but the survey does not address production loop engineering such as scorekeepers and guardrails.
- The Table 1 labels reflect its own judgment.

BUILDS ON: Holland (genetic algorithm [47]); AlphaGo/AlphaZero self-play (Silver et al [101,102]); Self-Instruct (Wang et al [127]); STaR (Zelikman [149]); ReST (Gulcehre [42]) and ReST-EM (Singh [103]); Self-Refine (Madaan [80]); Reflexion (Shinn [98]); Constitutional AI (Bai [9]); Self-Rewarding (Yuan [148]); LLM-as-a-Judge (Zheng [157]); Boud, Keogh and Walker (2013) on experiential learning.

CODE: none (a survey; equations only).

FIGURES
- Fig 2, p.3: conceptual framework. It shows the loop acquisition, refinement, updating, evaluation, with the evaluation output feeding the next objective E_{t+1}. It is the best single diagram for the note.
- Fig 3, p.6: taxonomy tree of all methods.
- Table 1, p.5: per-method matrix of task, solution, feedback, refinement, update (in-weight or in-context) and objective.
- Table 2, p.16: memory content (experience, rationale) and operations (insert, reflect, forget).
- Fig 4-8 (pp.8-14): task evolution, solution evolution, feedback types, refinement, update.
I did not run the captions script; I took the figure content from the extracted text.
